q-132345.worked_solution:
If $X∼\text{Exp}(\lambda )$ is an exponential random variable, then

$$
\text{E}[X]=\frac{1}{\lambda }.
$$

$$
\text{E}[X]=\frac{1}{9}
$$

q-132624.name: Question 3
q-132624.problem: The time $X,$ in seconds, between two students arriving at a canteen can be modeled as an exponential random variable $X∼\text{Exp}(0.05).$ If a student has just arrived at the canteen, what is the average time until the next student arrives there?
q-132624.worked_solution:
Recall that if $X∼\text{Exp}(\lambda )$ is an exponential random variable, then

$$
\text{E}[X]=\frac{1}{\lambda }.
$$

We're given that $X∼\text{Exp}(0.05).$ Therefore, $\lambda =0.05,$ and

$$
\text{E}[X]=\frac{1}{0.05}\,\text{sec}=20\,\text{sec}.
$$

Therefore, the average time until the next student arrives is $20$ seconds.

q-112757.name: Question 4
q-112757.problem: The time $X,$ in minutes, between two customers arriving at a bank can be modeled as an exponential random variable $X∼\text{Exp}(5).$ If a customer has just arrived at the bank, what is the average time until the next customer arrives at the bank?
q-112757.worked_solution:
Recall that if $X∼\text{Exp}(\lambda )$ is an exponential random variable, then

$$
\text{E}[X]=\frac{1}{\lambda }.
$$

We're given that $X∼\text{Exp}(5).$ Therefore, $\lambda =5,$ which means that $5$ customers arrive each minute. Hence,

$$
\text{E}[X]=\frac{1}{5}\,\text{min}=12\,\text{s}.
$$

Therefore, the average time until the next customer is $12$ seconds.

q-132438.name: Question 5
q-132438.worked_solution:
If $X∼\text{Exp}(\lambda )$ is an exponential random variable, then

$$
\text{SD}[X]=\sqrt{\text{Var}[X]}=\frac{1}{\lambda }.
$$

Therefore, for our random variable $X∼\text{Exp}(\frac{11}{23}),$ we have the following standard deviation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{SD}[X] & =\frac{1}{(\frac{11}{23})} \\  & =\frac{23}{11}\end{aligned}
$$

q-132438.html:
Question 5
?

Given that X∼Exp(1123), what is SD[X]?

a
1123
b
2311
c
211
d
123
e
111
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

If X∼Exp(λ) is an exponential random variable, then

SD[X]=Var[X]=1λ.

Therefore, for our random variable X∼Exp(1123), we have the following standard deviation: SD[X]=1(1123)=2311

q-132440.name: Question 6
q-132440.worked_solution:
If $X∼\text{Exp}(\lambda )$ is an exponential random variable, then

$$
\text{SD}[X]=\sqrt{\text{Var}[X]}=\frac{1}{\lambda }.
$$

Therefore, for our random variable $X∼\text{Exp}(\frac{5}{12}),$ we have the following standard deviation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{SD}[X] & =\frac{1}{(\frac{5}{12})} \\  & =\frac{12}{5}\end{aligned}
$$
